ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 4 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Frida Kahlo

code.originalText: Four-week chronic pain follow-up with the first opioid dose reduction

text.paragraph: Four-week chronic pain follow-up and first opioid dose reduction. [S]

Ms. Kahlo returns four weeks after her first visit. The cold she had last week has cleared. She has gone to physical therapy twice a week, missing one aquatic session while she was ill, and wears the new shoe lift. On duloxetine 60 mg for two weeks she has had no nausea, sweating, or dizziness. The burning in her right leg is less, and she now stands at the easel for about 20 minutes. She has kept to no more than four oxycodone tablets a day and on most days takes three or four. She is ready for the first dose reduction she agreed to two weeks ago, and she starts weekly cognitive behavioral therapy for chronic pain today. [S]

Long-term opioid therapy, first taper step (Z79.891). 60 MME a day with improving function and no sign of opioid use disorder: one prescriber on the prescription drug monitoring program, a consistent urine drug test at intake, and no early refills. [S]
Reduce oxycodone to 10 mg three times daily as needed and 5 mg at bedtime as needed, 52.5 MME a day.
Next reduction in about a month if pain and function hold; pause if they worsen.
Call for yawning, gooseflesh, stomach cramps, diarrhea, or restlessness, which would suggest withdrawal.
A lower dose means lower tolerance: never take extra tablets to make up a dose, and keep naloxone at hand.
